TITLE: Within-School Wealth Inequality and Learning Achievement: Evidence From PISA
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study uses PISA 2012, 2015, and 2018, two-level mixed-effects models, country fixed effects, sampling weights, replicate weights, plausible values, and robustness checks using reading outcomes, larger schools, and alternative inequality measures.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Methodologically adequate multi-cycle PISA inequality study
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study uses PISA 2012, 2015, and 2018, two-level mixed-effects models, country fixed effects, sampling weights, replicate weights, plausible values, and robustness checks using reading outcomes, larger schools, and alternative inequality measures. It reconstructs the 2012 wealth index using the later two-parameter IRT approach for cross-cycle consistency. Important limitations remain: the analysis is observational and does not identify causality; treatment of all plausible values and variance pooling should be confirmed in the published version and annexes; missing-data handling is not fully documented; and no code repository or replication package was identified. The Research Square preprint was used for assessment, but the final citation must use the 2025 Review of Income and Wealth article, DOI 10.1111/roiw.70040.

TITLE: Performance decline in a low‐stakes test at age 15 and educational attainment at age 25: Cross‐country longitudinal evidence
AUTHORS: Francesca Borgonovi; Alessandro Ferrara; M. Piacentini
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study links PISA 2000 or 2003 participants to longitudinal outcomes at ages 25 to 27 in Australia, Denmark, and Switzerland.
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study links PISA 2000 or 2003 participants to longitudinal outcomes at ages 25 to 27 in Australia, Denmark, and Switzerland. It applies PISA sampling and replication weights, combines them with longitudinal follow-up weights, clusters standard errors by school, models item and booklet effects, and reports robustness checks. Important limitations include attrition of 36 percent response in Australia and 44 percent in Denmark, limited country diversity, different PISA major domains, and an associational rather than causal design.

TITLE: Факторы, влияющие на достижения Казахстанских учащихся в международном исследовании PISA-2018
AUTHORS: Оспанова Улжан Абаевна; K. Nurumov; M. Atanaeva
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study evaluates mathematics, reading and science achievement among Kazakhstani students using PISA 2018.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Adequate multilevel PISA analysis using plausible values and complex sample design
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study evaluates mathematics, reading and science achievement among Kazakhstani students using PISA 2018. It explicitly reports multilevel regression analysis, plausible values and complex sample-design procedures, and separates individual, school and regional factors. It remains an observational single-country analysis and does not identify causal effects. Missing-data treatment and replication materials are not sufficiently clear, but the methodological alignment with PISA makes it a final candidate.

TITLE: Education for Growth: Why and For Whom?
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study compares Barro-Lee, Kyriacou and World Values Survey education measures and demonstrates severe attenuation from measurement error in first-differenced country data.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Strong methodological analysis of measurement error and heterogeneity in education-growth models
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study compares Barro-Lee, Kyriacou and World Values Survey education measures and demonstrates severe attenuation from measurement error in first-differenced country data. It evaluates alternative time windows, instrumental variables, capital controls, non-linearity and heterogeneous country coefficients. It explicitly warns that reverse causality and omitted policies prevent simple causal interpretation. The careful treatment of measurement error and specification sensitivity makes it a strong methodological reference.

TITLE: Who Makes It Into PISA? Understanding the Impact of PISA Sample Eligibility Using Turkey as a Case Study (PISA 2003 - PISA 2012)
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The OECD study examines Turkey across PISA 2003 to 2012 and shows that eligibility rose from approximately 45 percent to 80 percent.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Strong analysis of PISA eligibility, coverage and changing sample composition
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The OECD study examines Turkey across PISA 2003 to 2012 and shows that eligibility rose from approximately 45 percent to 80 percent. It combines PISA and Demographic and Health Survey data, uses survey weighting, five plausible values, composite standard errors and multiple robustness checks. The study directly demonstrates how changing sample coverage can bias trend interpretation. It is limited to one national case and does not estimate a causal intervention effect, but it is essential for interpreting international assessment trends.

TITLE: The geography of tertiary education inequality in Europe: a within- and cross-country analysis over time
AUTHORS: Fabrizio Bernardi; Ilaria Lievore; Manuel Tomás Valdés
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study combines European Social Survey waves 1 to 10 and analyzes 285,506 individuals in 298 regions from 25 European countries.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Large harmonized European Social Survey analysis with multilevel regional and country comparisons
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study combines European Social Survey waves 1 to 10 and analyzes 285,506 individuals in 298 regions from 25 European countries. It uses multilevel linear probability models, country-specific regressions, intraclass correlations and residual diagnostics. The large harmonized sample and explicit regional structure support inclusion. Limitations include observational repeated cross-sectional data, possible differences in regional coding across survey rounds, and limited support for causal interpretation.

TITLE: The Century of Education
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study constructs a historical educational-attainment database for 74 countries from 1870 to 2010.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Strong long-run attainment database with explicit measurement-error and robustness analysis
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study constructs a historical educational-attainment database for 74 countries from 1870 to 2010. It documents missing enrollment data, imputation, measurement error, differential mortality bias and multiple robustness experiments. Some early observations rely on neighboring countries and constructed historical values, so uncertainty is substantial before 1960. Its transparent treatment of measurement limitations and convergence makes it a strong methodological and substantive reference.

TITLE: Does schooling actually perpetuate educational inequality in mathematics performance? A validity question on the measures of opportunity to learn in PISA
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study reexamines PISA 2012 data and evaluates the construct validity of opportunity-to-learn indicators.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Strong methodological assessment of construct validity in PISA opportunity-to-learn measurement
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study reexamines PISA 2012 data and evaluates the construct validity of opportunity-to-learn indicators. It identifies construct-irrelevant variance and separates two latent dimensions that challenge earlier mediation claims. The cross-country probability samples and explicit measurement critique make it methodologically relevant. Because the design is observational and cross-sectional, the reported relationships should not be interpreted causally.

TITLE: Improving the estimation of educational attainment: New methods for assessing average years of schooling from binned data
AUTHORS: Joseph R. Friedman; Nicholas Graetz; Emmanuela E. Gakidou
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: Using 1,680 survey and census datasets, the study compares the standard-duration method with new models for splitting binned schooling data.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Strong out-of-sample validation of educational-attainment measurement methods
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: Using 1,680 survey and census datasets, the study compares the standard-duration method with new models for splitting binned schooling data. It uses out-of-sample predictive validation and reports materially lower error for the space-time approach. The PDF uses a custom character encoding that affected text extraction, but its identity and results were manually confirmed. It is directly relevant to measurement quality and predictive validation.

TITLE: Differences in educational attainment by country of origin: Evidence from Australia
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study uses the nationally representative 2003 Longitudinal Survey of Australian Youth cohort derived from PISA, including 10,370 participants.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: National longitudinal cohort analysis with sampling and attrition weights, probit models and robustness checks
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study uses the nationally representative 2003 Longitudinal Survey of Australian Youth cohort derived from PISA, including 10,370 participants. It estimates probit models, reports average marginal effects, applies weights for initial sampling and later attrition, uses robust standard errors and conducts subgroup robustness analyses. Limitations include observational identification, incomplete country-of-origin indicators and possible residual attrition or omitted-variable bias.

TITLE: The Intraclass Correlation Coefficient as a Measure of Educational Inequality: An Empirical Study with Data from PISA 2018
AUTHORS: Yasemin YARDIM; Gürkan CÜVİTOĞLU; Burak AYDIN
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The preprint analyzes 79 PISA 2018 systems using ten plausible values, student and school weights, multilevel models, FIML for missing data and meta-analysis of ICCs.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Strong multilevel PISA analysis with plausible values, weights, missing-data treatment and meta-analysis
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The preprint analyzes 79 PISA 2018 systems using ten plausible values, student and school weights, multilevel models, FIML for missing data and meta-analysis of ICCs. Results from plausible values are combined using multiple-imputation procedures. The main limitations are its observational design, sensitivity of ICC interpretation and preprint status. Methodologically it is a strong candidate for educational-inequality analysis.

TITLE: Socioeconomic Inequalities in Reading Literacy and Learning-Related Characteristics: Evidence from PISA 2022
SCOPE_OR_SAMPLE_EVIDENCE: The study analyzes 52,392 students from ten Asian economies using ten reading plausible values, final student weights and 80 replicate weights.
FULL_TEXT_REASON: Technically adequate PISA 2022 comparative analysis with plausible values and replicate weights
ASSESSMENT_NOTES: The study analyzes 52,392 students from ten Asian economies using ten reading plausible values, final student weights and 80 replicate weights. It estimates each plausible value and combines results, explicitly avoids causal interpretation and checks the effect of complete-case exclusion. Remaining limitations include self-reported predictors, observational associations and possible residual selection from missing data.
